issues.description: Attribute type for 'lectureName' is inconsistent: the problem statement and UML specify lectureName as a String, and the template expects students to add that attribute, but the solution repository defines a separate LectureName class and uses LectureName as the type for the lectureName field. This divergence will confuse students about the expected type and API and prevents straightforward implementation according to the exercise specification.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the type of lectureName consistent across artifacts. Either change the solution to use a plain String for lectureName (remove LectureName class and use String in the field, constructor parameter, getters and setters), or update the problem statement and UML to explicitly require and explain a LectureName value object. Preferably revert the solution to use String to match the UML and template guidance.

issues.description: The solution implementation has method/field type inconsistencies: the Lecture class field 'lectureName' is declared as LectureName, but the getter and setter signatures in the same class use String. This internal mismatch causes compile errors and is structurally incorrect.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the types within the Lecture class. If lectureName should be a LectureName object, change the getter and setter signatures to return and accept LectureName. If lectureName should be String (as per the problem/UML), change the field and constructor parameter to String and remove or adapt the LectureName class. Ensure constructor, field, getters and setters all use the same type.

issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify a lectureName attribute of type String (attribute name: lectureName) and expect constructor/getter/setter to use this String. The solution introduces a new class LectureName and changes the Lecture constructor and field to use LectureName (and adds a LectureName.java). This renaming/type change (String -> LectureName) breaks the direct mapping between the problem/template requirements and the solution API and will confuse students about the expected type and constructor signature.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the representation of the lecture name consistent across artifacts. Either (A) revert the solution to use a plain String for lectureName and a constructor parameter of type String (e.g., public Lecture(String lectureName, ...)) and remove LectureName.java, or (B) update the problem statement and template to explicitly require a LectureName type (adjust UML and method signatures) so all artifacts use LectureName consistently. Prefer option A to minimize student cognitive load.
